title: Phil 2009 1969 sugarcane (Phil 09 1969): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Phil 2009 1969 sugarcane is a sugarcane variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Phil 2009 1969 is a registered sugarcane variety, also sold or known as Phil 09 1969 or NSIC Sc 15. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2022 as NSIC 2022 Sc 15. Sugar Regulatory Administration bred it. It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest, with 241.45 LKg of sugar per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Phil 09 1969 or NSIC Sc 15, this is the same sugarcane. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [sugarcane variety finder](/crop-varieties/sugarcane), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for sugarcane](/land-preparation/sugarcane-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 8 months from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 241.45 LKg of sugar per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Phil 2009 1969 sugarcane takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. That is 2.8 months faster than the average of the 16 sugarcane varieties with a day count, 10.8 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 241.45 LKg/ha beats the average of its group, 160.71. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Sugar yield is counted in LKg, bags of 50 kilograms of raw sugar per hectare. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew).

The pests and diseases that hit sugarcane fields most often: [Rice field rats](/pests/rice-field-rats), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [white grub](/pests/white-grub). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its stalks grew about 281 cm long and 3.32 cm thick. Trash: self detrashing, which decides how much cleaning the cane needs before milling.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Erect, self detrashing, stalks about 281 cm, 3.32 cm thick, 2.48 kg.
Resistant to downy mildew, leaf scorch, smut and yellow spot.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a 2022 SRA release with the highest average sugar yield in the NSIC sugarcane list. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Phil 2009 1969 sugarcane

Mills pay for sugar, not cane, so compare the sugar yield in LKg per hectare as well as the tonnes of cane. Pick a variety that ratoons well, and one rated against smut and downy mildew, the diseases that cut a ratoon crop short. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation in the Philippines](/land-preparation/land-preparation-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is Phil 09 1969 the same as Phil 2009 1969?
items.a: Yes. Phil 09 1969 is another name for Phil 2009 1969, registered as NSIC 2022 Sc 15. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 241.45 LKg of sugar per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Phil 2009 1969?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
